caption: Fig. 1. Open in a new tab Epidermal cyst. When imaged at 13 MHz, the lesion appears as a non-specific, subcutaneous, hypoechoic nodule without Doppler signals ( a ). When using a 22 MHz probe, the cystic duct becomes evident, allowing a definitive diagnosis ( b )

Fig. 2. Open in a new tab Pericicatricial seroma in a patient with recent melanoma exeresis. If scanned at 13 MHz, the lesion appears as a small, avascular, non-specific nodule ( a ). When imaged at 22 MHz, the lesion is clearly anechoic ( b )

Fig. 3. Open in a new tab Sagittal extended field-of-view scan of the chest. A xiphoid appendix plasmacytoma mass—hypoechoic, ill-defined, and heterogeneous—is optimally displayed at the tip of the sternum
Fig. 4. Open in a new tab Sarcoma of the tight. Proper measurement of the mass requires tracing the largest diameter and the largest diameter perpendicular to the former (34 × 19 mm)
Fig. 5. Open in a new tab Locally recurring leg sarcoma. Directional power-Doppler scan. Heterogeneous, hypoechoic nodule with peripheral vascularization
Fig. 6. Open in a new tab Young butcher with wrist swelling 4 months after a knife wound. Patient photograph ( a ). Color-Doppler scan depicts a radial artery pseudoaneurysm ( b )

Fig. 7. Open in a new tab Abdominal wall desmoid tumor. Ill-defined, heterogeneous mass within the rectus muscle. The lesion is mostly stiff at elastography (red and brown colors of the elasticity scale)

Fig. 8. Open in a new tab Non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma presenting as an elbow mass. The enlarged epitrochlear lymph node exhibits some irregular, peripheral flow at directional power-Doppler imaging ( s ). Discrete, heterogeneous contrast enhancement is seen during the arterial phase of CEUS (13 s after contrast medium injection, b ). Marked wash-out is noted during the venous phase (63 s after contrast medium injection, c )
Fig. 9. Open in a new tab The risk of malignancy increases with the depth of the lesion location. Drawing from Galant et al. [ 46 ], modified
Fig. 10. Open in a new tab Forearm aggressive fibromatosis encasing the radial artery. Color-Doppler scan
Fig. 11. Open in a new tab Axillary recurrence of breast cancer with infiltration of the axillary nerve (arrows)

Fig. 12. Open in a new tab Palpable axillary mass. The classical snowstorm pattern indicates silicone-filled lymph nodes due to breast implant rupture. The patient was unaware of the rupture of the prosthesis before US and mentioned the presence of the implant only when asked

Fig. 13. Open in a new tab Palpable mass of the hand dorsum. Painless, four-day lasting swelling in an elderly woman ( a ). US shows fluid effusion around the extensor tendons due to tenosynovitis ( b )

Fig. 14. Open in a new tab Giant-cell tendon sheath tumor of the small finger. X-ray shows dorsal swelling of the distal phalanx, with no calcifications or bony change ( a ). Power-Doppler scans showed a bilobed hypoechoic nodule without significant flow signals ( b )

Fig. 15. Open in a new tab Palpable, painless thigh nodule in a 9-year-old boy. The classical appearance of a heterogeneous, subcutaneous nodule with hyperechoic, near-calcified center and hypoechoic halo ( a ) and with discrete intralesional flows at directional power-Doppler ( b ) should be diagnosed as a pilomatricoma
